1	---
2	name: mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world
3	description: "New AniRacers world built from a real Bambu-Studio 3MF mesh of Mishkenot Zvulun, Netanya (replaces procedural OSM approach for this map)"
4	metadata: 
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: bce79f60-02bd-4173-ac40-7fe9dd8efb15
8	---
9	
10	The user is building a second AniRacers world: **Mishkenot Zvulun, Netanya, Israel** (seaside residential neighborhood by Netanya Academic College; pin 32.309930, 34.880891 on HaRav Toledano). Instead of the procedural OSM pipeline used for [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]], this world comes from a **real 3D mesh the user exported as a 3MF**.
11	
12	**Source of truth:** `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/Full.3mf` (49 MB). It's a Bambu Studio multi-color **3D-print** model: 25 "Puzzle Pieces" tiles, all sharing one identity build transform (translate +128,128,0 on a 256 mm bed) — so pieces are modeled **in-place** and interlock; no per-piece reassembly needed. Geometry is one big `3D/Objects/object-1.model` (XML, stored uncompressed in the zip). Two earlier exports also exist: `mishkenot_zvulun.3mf` (no trees, 130k tris) and `mishkenot_zvulun_with_trees.3mf` (90 MB, 1.18M tris). **Use Full.3mf.**
13	
14	**Segmentation = already done, by filament colour (extruder).** 8 colours → roles, total **761,180 tris**:
15	ground `#ffffff` (133k) · lawn `#4ade80` (99k) · sidewalk `#9ca3af` (41k) · road `#262626` (63k) · building `#b8b8b8` (12k, tall low-poly boxes) · grass `#0fe300` (25k) · **tree `#7fb35d` (388k = half the model)** · water `#3399ff` (52). So "color buildings/roads/etc." is just assigning a game material per part.
16	
17	**Converter:** `scripts/convert-3mf-world.mjs <extractedDir> <outDir>` — unzip the 3mf first, then it maps each leaf `<object>` → extruder (via `Metadata/model_settings.config` part id→extruder, colours in `project_settings.config`), merges by extruder, writes `assets/mishkenot/world.bin` (f32 positions then u32 indices; indices rebased per-part-local) + `world.json` (manifest: bbox, per-part role/color/vStart/vCount/iStart/iCount). 13 MB bin. Coords kept in **source mm, Z-up**; game must re-centre via bbox and swap Z-up→Y-up and rescale (world ≈ 108.6×149.8×13.5 mm). `scripts/preview-mesh-world.mjs` headless-renders it for sanity.
18	
19	**Integrated** into `index.html` as the `mishkenot` world: `buildMishkenotWorld()` (async-loads `/assets/mishkenot/world.{json,bin}`, builds 8 meshes), `MISHKENOT_CTRL`, `VTHEME.mishkenot`, a NETANYA GP start button (`startMishkenot`), a `buildWorld` branch, and a `?world=<name>` deep-link/headless hook. Verify in-game with `scripts/verify-mishkenot.mjs` (deep-links `?world=mishkenot&dbg`, writes `_ingame_overview/_top/_live.png`). It now renders faithfully (matches the satellite top-down).
20	
21	**Integration gotchas (hard-won — the first attempts looked "terrible"):** (1) the generic road ribbon + its big GREEN ground plane are built once at load for the Castle loop and sit on top — `trackMeshes.forEach(m=>m.visible=false)` in buildMishkenotWorld. (2) the pale building/ground colours blow out under the default sun — dim `hemi.intensity=0.55; sun.intensity=0.95`. (3) the mesh has its OWN solid ground slab (~7 game-units thick); any extra base plane must sit BELOW it (`y=-9`) or it hides the neighbourhood ground. Transform: scale 1.33, `rotation.x=-90` (Z-up→Y-up), `position=(-S*cx,-S*zref,S*cy)` with `zref`=road part top so streets land at y≈0. Buildings get per-building vertex-colour tints.
22	
23	**Scale rebuild (current approach):** the user wanted houses realistically large vs the kart (~10×). The 3MF is print-scaled (no real units), so buildings now come from `assets/mishkenot/buildings.glb` (= `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/Mishkenot_zvulun2.glb`, copied in), which is in **real metres** (~423×566 m footprint, up to ~52 m tall). Loaded at **1 game-unit = 1 metre** (`MISH_SCALE=1.0`) so the ~3.8 m kart is dwarfed. The GLB is buildings-only/monochrome (`THREE.GLTFExporter`, 402 meshes, all `#565a5d`, no roads/grass/trees) — so `buildMishkenotWorld` recolours each building with tints and **grafts the trees from the 3MF `world.bin` tree part**, fitted by bbox into the GLB footprint. Added `GLTFLoader` via `unpkg three@0.128.0/examples/js/loaders/GLTFLoader.js`.
24	
25	**GLB axis gotcha:** GLTFLoader honours the file's node transform, so the GLB loads **Y-up** (height in Y), while the 3MF is **Z-up**. Do NOT re-rotate the GLB. When grafting 3MF trees, map 3MF(x,y,z) → GLB(x, height=y, z): 3MF-z(height)→GLB-y, 3MF-y→GLB-z.
26	
27	**Status / next:** GLB buildings + grafted trees render upright at correct human scale (verified). The GLB has **no roads/grass** (open green ground for now). PENDING: the **race track is still a provisional loop** (`MISHKENOT_CTRL`, scaled to the metre world) — route onto real streets; optionally add roads/ground detail. Track route is the user's call. Keep the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]].
28

Everything's prepped while the build finishes downloading the JOGL dependencies in the background. Here's where things stand:

**Repo assessment so far (from reading the source):**
- **OSM2World** is an MIT-licensed Java/Maven CLI. The `convert` subcommand reads OSM data (a file, or live from the Overpass API) and writes **`.glb` directly** — the exact format the game already loads via `GLTFLoader` (same path as the Mishkenot world).
- The GLB is emitted **Y-up, in real metres** (`x, y, −z`), three.js's native convention — so **no axis rotation needed** on integration, unlike the 3MF pipeline.
- Run model: `java -jar osm2world-desktop-….jar convert -i <osm> -o <glb> --lod 4` (manifest already wires the main class + `lib/` classpath).

**Done already:**
- Maven fetched & building OSM2World.jar (JDK 17, the project's target) — *in progress*.
- Downloaded the **Eiffel Tower / Champ de Mars** OSM extract (71,411 nodes · 8,643 ways · 152 Eiffel refs) → `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/eiffel.osm`.
- Wrote `scripts/preview-osm2world.mjs` — a headless GLB renderer (three.js r128 + GLTFLoader 0.128) that reports triangle/material/bbox stats and shoots a 3/4 + top-down PNG.

I'll fire the conversion and preview the moment the jar lands. The build is pulling jogamp libs (slow mirror), so it's a few more minutes — I'll continue automatically when it completes.

content.text:
Critical finding: `OSMFileReader` is a `record` that does **not** override `getData(LatLonBounds)` — the interface default **ignores the bbox and returns all data**. So `--input_bbox` won't clip a file; I must bound it at the Overpass query. My query's `>;` ("recurse down") dragged in entire city-wide route/river **relation** members. 

I'll re-query recursing only *way-nodes* (`node(w)`), not relation members — that keeps in-bbox relations (like the tower) without pulling geometry across Paris.

Verdict: **viable and lower-effort than the hand-built [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]] or the [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]] mesh-wrangling** — it auto-produces a recognizable real place. Outputs **GLB that is Y-up, real metres, `(x,y,-z)`** → drops straight into the game's existing GLTFLoader path (same as Mishkenot), no axis rotation.

**Build (one-time, env-specific):** Maven was NOT installed (only JDK present). Downloaded Maven 3.9.9 zip to `C:\Users\YonatanSetbon\tools\apache-maven-3.9.9\`. Build with **JDK 17** (`C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17`, the project's target; JDK 14/17/24 all present). Skipping `-am`'s `core-web` (TeaVM Java→JS) module avoids a long, fragile step. Output: `OSM2World/desktop/target/osm2world-desktop-0.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` + `target/lib/` (121 jars; manifest Class-Path already wired). Main class `org.osm2world.console.OSM2World`.

**Convert:** `java [--add-exports java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED ...] -jar <jar> convert -i <in.osm> -o <out.glb> --lod 0..4`. Reads an OSM file or live Overpass (`--input_mode OVERPASS`); `convert` always requires `-i` so file input is simplest. Default config emits **flat-shaded solid-color geometry, only ~2 materials, NO textures** — boxy extruded buildings with real roof shapes = reads as blocky/low-poly, compatible-ish with the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (recolor the 2 materials to the palette; karts/animals stay voxel).

content.text:
Done — I went end-to-end: built the repo, generated a real Eiffel Tower world from it, rendered it, and compared detail levels. Here's the verdict.

## Is OSM2World good for AniRacers? **Yes — viable, and less manual work than your other two worlds.**

I built `OSM2World.jar` from the vendored repo (had to install Maven; used JDK 17), pulled the Eiffel Tower / Champ de Mars area from OpenStreetMap, and converted it. The renders above are that output — **the actual Eiffel Tower, red-roofed Haussmann blocks, the Champ de Mars lawns and fountain basins, Trocadéro gardens across the river** — all generated automatically, zero hand-modeling.

**What makes it a good fit**
- **Output format is exactly what the game wants**: GLB, **Y-up, real metres** — drops straight into your existing `GLTFLoader` path (same as the Mishkenot world), *no axis rotation*.
- **Looks blockish, not realistic**: default config emits flat-shaded, solid-color extruded buildings with real roof shapes — only **2 materials**, no textures. It's not voxel, but it's boxy/low-poly and easy to recolor to your palette. Karts/animals/props stay voxel (per [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]]).
- **Tunable cost** — this is the key number:

  | LOD | Triangles | Size |
  |-----|-----------|------|
  | LOD4 | 1.82M | 193 MB ❌ too heavy |
  | **LOD2** | **128k** | **18 MB** ✅ ships, looks ~identical |
  | LOD1/0 | ~50k | ~12 MB |

  (Your Mishkenot world is ~761k tris, so LOD2 is *light*.)
- **MIT-licensed**, ~25s per conversion, **any place on Earth** by changing the bbox, and the **real road network is in the data** — so the kart track can be routed onto actual streets (the open TODO on Mishkenot).

**The real caveats (all solvable)**
1. **Clipping is fiddly.** `--input_bbox` is silently ignored for file input, and ways crossing the bbox edge leave "comet-tail" line artifacts (visible streaking off the model). Production needs a real geometric clip — OSM2World's `--tile` mode clips cleanly, or clip the GLB to the bbox after.
2. **Build setup** is a one-time chore (Maven + JDK17; skip the `core-web`/javadoc modules or it's slow). Done now.
3. **Mesh is ~3,700 small meshes** — should be merged by material for three.js draw-call perf.
4. It's *generated*, not art-directed — needs a recolor pass to look intentional.

**My recommendation:** adopt it as the world-base generator. The production recipe would be: **LOD1/LOD2 → clip to bbox → merge by material → recolor to the AniRacers palette → route the track on real roads.**

Artifacts are in `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/` (kept `eiffel_lod{0,1,2}.glb` + previews; deleted the 193 MB LOD4s, regenerable in 25s). Previewer: `node scripts/preview-osm2world.mjs <glb>`.

Want me to take the next step — wire a clipped **"Paris GP"** LOD2 world into `index.html` as a third world (recolored + track routed), or stop here since the evaluation's done? I'd lean toward doing one fully-integrated Paris world so you can drive it and judge it in-game.

Output: `OSM2World/desktop/target/osm2world-desktop-0.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` + `target/lib/` (121 jars; manifest Class-Path already wired). Main class `org.osm2world.console.OSM2World`.

**Convert:** `java [--add-exports java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED ...] -jar <jar> convert -i <in.osm> -o <out.glb> --lod 0..4`. Reads an OSM file or live Overpass (`--input_mode OVERPASS`); `convert` always requires `-i` so file input is simplest. Default config emits **flat-shaded solid-color geometry, only ~2 materials, NO textures** — boxy extruded buildings with real roof shapes = reads as blocky/low-poly, compatible-ish with the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (recolor the 2 materials to the palette; karts/animals stay voxel).

**LOD is the cost knob (Eiffel ~700m bbox):** LOD4 = 1.82M tris / **193 MB** (too heavy for web — every tree a 3D model, full Eiffel lattice, facade detail); **LOD2 = 128k tris / 18 MB** (visually ~identical at gameplay distance, the keeper); LOD1/LOD0 ≈ 12 MB. name: osm2world-world-pipeline
description: "OSM2World (vendored Java repo) evaluated as a from-OSM world-geometry generator for AniRacers — build + convert recipe, LOD sizes, gotchas"

OSM2World (`OSM2World/`, MIT, Java/Maven, v0.5.0-SNAPSHOT) was vendored and evaluated on 2026-06-18 as a candidate generator for AniRacers race worlds, using the **Eiffel Tower / Champ de Mars** area as a test. Verdict: **viable and lower-effort than the hand-built [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]] or the [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]] mesh-wrangling** — it auto-produces a recognizable real place. Outputs **GLB that is Y-up, real metres, `(x,y,-z)`** → drops straight into the game's existing GLTFLoader path (same as Mishkenot), no axis rotation.

**Build (one-time, env-specific):** Maven was NOT installed (only JDK present). Downloaded Maven 3.9.9 zip to `C:\Users\YonatanSetbon\tools\apache-maven-3.9.9\`. Build with **JDK 17** (`C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17`, the project's target; JDK 14/17/24 all present). The CLI lives in the `desktop` module; build only what's needed and skip the slow/fragile bits: `mvn -f OSM2World/pom.xml -pl desktop -am -DskipTests -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true package` (run via PowerShell `--%` stop-parsing or the `-D` args get mangled). Skipping `-am`'s `core-web` (TeaVM Java→JS) module avoids a long, fragile step. Output: `OSM2World/desktop/target/osm2world-desktop-0.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` + `target/lib/` (121 jars; manifest Class-Path already wired). Main class `org.osm2world.console.OSM2World`.

**Convert:** `java [--add-exports java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED ...] -jar <jar> convert -i <in.osm> -o <out.glb> --lod 0..4`. Reads an OSM file or live Overpass (`--input_mode OVERPASS`); `convert` always requires `-i` so file input is simplest. Default config emits **flat-shaded solid-color geometry, only ~2 materials, NO textures** — boxy extruded buildings with real roof shapes = reads as blocky/low-poly, compatible-ish with the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (recolor the 2 materials to the palette; karts/animals stay voxel).

**LOD is the cost knob (Eiffel ~700m bbox):** LOD4 = 1.82M tris / **193 MB** (too heavy for web — every tree a 3D model, full Eiffel lattice, facade detail); **LOD2 = 128k tris / 18 MB** (visually ~identical at gameplay distance, the keeper); LOD1/LOD0 ≈ 12 MB. Convert ≈ 20–30s. Game already runs the ~761k-tri Mishkenot world, so LOD2 is light.

**Gotchas:** (1) `OSMFileReader` is a record that does NOT override `getData(LatLonBounds)` → **`--input_bbox` is ignored for file input**; you must bound at the Overpass query. (2) `way(bbox)`/`>;` recursion drags in city-wide route/river **relation** members (first try = 10km extent, 183MB). Use `node(w)` recursion not `>;`, and drop or non-recurse relations. (3) Even then, complete ways crossing the bbox edge leave "comet-tail" line artifacts beyond the area — needs a real geometric clip (clip GLB to bbox, or use OSM2World `--tile` mode which clips) for production. (4) Mesh is many small meshes (~3700) — merge by material for three.js draw-call perf.

**Test artifacts (git-ignored, untracked):** `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/` has `eiffel.osm` (over-broad), `eiffel2.osm` (clipped via `node(w)`), `eiffel_lod{0,1,2}.glb`, preview PNGs. The user is building a second AniRacers world: **Mishkenot Zvulun, Netanya, Israel** (seaside residential neighborhood by Netanya Academic College; pin 32.309930, 34.880891 on HaRav Toledano). Instead of the procedural OSM pipeline used for [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]], this world comes from a **real 3D mesh the user exported as a 3MF**.

**Source of truth:** `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/Full.3mf` (49 MB). It's a Bambu Studio multi-color **3D-print** model: 25 "Puzzle Pieces" tiles, all sharing one identity build transform (translate +128,128,0 on a 256 mm bed) — so pieces are modeled **in-place** and interlock; no per-piece reassembly needed. Geometry is one big `3D/Objects/object-1.model` (XML, stored uncompressed in the zip). Two earlier exports also exist: `mishkenot_zvulun.3mf` (no trees, 130k tris) and `mishkenot_zvulun_with_trees.3mf` (90 MB, 1.18M tris). **Use Full.3mf.**

**Segmentation = already done, by filament colour (extruder).** 8 colours → roles, total **761,180 tris**:
ground `#ffffff` (133k) · lawn `#4ade80` (99k) · sidewalk `#9ca3af` (41k) · road `#262626` (63k) · building `#b8b8b8` (12k, tall low-poly boxes) · grass `#0fe300` (25k) · **tree `#7fb35d` (388k = half the model)** · water `#3399ff` (52). So "color buildings/roads/etc." is just assigning a game material per part.

**Converter:** `scripts/convert-3mf-world.mjs <extractedDir> <outDir>` — unzip the 3mf first, then it maps each leaf `<object>` → extruder (via `Metadata/model_settings.config` part id→extruder, colours in `project_settings.config`), merges by extruder, writes `assets/mishkenot/world.bin` (f32 positions then u32 indices; indices rebased per-part-local) + `world.json` (manifest: bbox, per-part role/color/vStart/vCount/iStart/iCount). 13 MB bin. Coords kept in **source mm, Z-up**; game must re-centre via bbox and swap Z-up→Y-up and rescale (world ≈ 108.6×149.8×13.5 mm). `scripts/preview-mesh-world.mjs` headless-renders it for sanity.

**Integrated** into `index.html` as the `mishkenot` world: `buildMishkenotWorld()` (async-loads `/assets/mishkenot/world.{json,bin}`, builds 8 meshes), `MISHKENOT_CTRL`, `VTHEME.mishkenot`, a NETANYA GP start button (`startMishkenot`), a `buildWorld` branch, and a `?world=<name>` deep-link/headless hook. Verify in-game with `scripts/verify-mishkenot.mjs` (deep-links `?world=mishkenot&dbg`, writes `_ingame_overview/_top/_live.png`). It now renders faithfully (matches the satellite top-down).

**Integration gotchas (hard-won — the first attempts looked "terrible"):** (1) the generic road ribbon + its big GREEN ground plane are built once at load for the Castle loop and sit on top — `trackMeshes.forEach(m=>m.visible=false)` in buildMishkenotWorld. (2) the pale building/ground colours blow out under the default sun — dim `hemi.intensity=0.55; sun.intensity=0.95`. (3) the mesh has its OWN solid ground slab (~7 game-units thick); any extra base plane must sit BELOW it (`y=-9`) or it hides the neighbourhood ground. Transform: scale 1.33, `rotation.x=-90` (Z-up→Y-up), `position=(-S*cx,-S*zref,S*cy)` with `zref`=road part top so streets land at y≈0. Buildings get per-building vertex-colour tints.

**Scale rebuild (current approach):** the user wanted houses realistically large vs the kart (~10×). The 3MF is print-scaled (no real units), so buildings now come from `assets/mishkenot/buildings.glb` (= `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/Mishkenot_zvulun2.glb`, copied in), which is in **real metres** (~423×566 m footprint, up to ~52 m tall). Loaded at **1 game-unit = 1 metre** (`MISH_SCALE=1.0`) so the ~3.8 m kart is dwarfed. The GLB is buildings-only/monochrome (`THREE.GLTFExporter`, 402 meshes, all `#565a5d`, no roads/grass/trees) — so `buildMishkenotWorld` recolours each building with tints and **grafts the trees from the 3MF `world.bin` tree part**, fitted by bbox into the GLB footprint. Added `GLTFLoader` via `unpkg three@0.128.0/examples/js/loaders/GLTFLoader.js`.

**GLB axis gotcha:** GLTFLoader honours the file's node transform, so the GLB loads **Y-up** (height in Y), while the 3MF is **Z-up**. Do NOT re-rotate the GLB. When grafting 3MF trees, map 3MF(x,y,z) → GLB(x, height=y, z): 3MF-z(height)→GLB-y, 3MF-y→GLB-z.

**Status / next:** GLB buildings + grafted trees render upright at correct human scale (verified). The GLB has **no roads/grass** (open green ground for now). Keep the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]].

---
name: osm2world-world-pipeline
description: "OSM2World (vendored Java repo) evaluated as a from-OSM world-geometry generator for AniRacers — build + convert recipe, LOD sizes, gotchas"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d45cbd15-7c08-4d07-9f7e-9203188d7f9f
---

OSM2World (`OSM2World/`, MIT, Java/Maven, v0.5.0-SNAPSHOT) was vendored and evaluated on 2026-06-18 as a candidate generator for AniRacers race worlds, using the **Eiffel Tower / Champ de Mars** area as a test. Verdict: **viable and lower-effort than the hand-built [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]] or the [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]] mesh-wrangling** — it auto-produces a recognizable real place. Outputs **GLB that is Y-up, real metres, `(x,y,-z)`** → drops straight into the game's existing GLTFLoader path (same as Mishkenot), no axis rotation.

**Build (one-time, env-specific):** Maven was NOT installed (only JDK present). Downloaded Maven 3.9.9 zip to `C:\Users\YonatanSetbon\tools\apache-maven-3.9.9\`. Build with **JDK 17** (`C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17`, the project's target; JDK 14/17/24 all present). The CLI lives in the `desktop` module; build only what's needed and skip the slow/fragile bits: `mvn -f OSM2World/pom.xml -pl desktop -am -DskipTests -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true package` (run via PowerShell `--%` stop-parsing or the `-D` args get mangled). Skipping `-am`'s `core-web` (TeaVM Java→JS) module avoids a long, fragile step. Output: `OSM2World/desktop/target/osm2world-desktop-0.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` + `target/lib/` (121 jars; manifest Class-Path already wired). Main class `org.osm2world.console.OSM2World`.

**Convert:** `java [--add-exports java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED ...] -jar <jar> convert -i <in.osm> -o <out.glb> --lod 0..4`. Reads an OSM file or live Overpass (`--input_mode OVERPASS`); `convert` always requires `-i` so file input is simplest. Default config emits **flat-shaded solid-color geometry, only ~2 materials, NO textures** — boxy extruded buildings with real roof shapes = reads as blocky/low-poly, compatible-ish with the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (recolor the 2 materials to the palette; karts/animals stay voxel).

**LOD is the cost knob (Eiffel ~700m bbox):** LOD4 = 1.82M tris / **193 MB** (too heavy for web — every tree a 3D model, full Eiffel lattice, facade detail); **LOD2 = 128k tris / 18 MB** (visually ~identical at gameplay distance, the keeper); LOD1/LOD0 ≈ 12 MB. Convert ≈ 20–30s. Game already runs the ~761k-tri Mishkenot world, so LOD2 is light.

**Gotchas:** (1) `OSMFileReader` is a record that does NOT override `getData(LatLonBounds)` → **`--input_bbox` is ignored for file input**; you must bound at the Overpass query. (2) `way(bbox)`/`>;` recursion drags in city-wide route/river **relation** members (first try = 10km extent, 183MB). Use `node(w)` recursion not `>;`, and drop or non-recurse relations. (3) Even then, complete ways crossing the bbox edge leave "comet-tail" line artifacts beyond the area — needs a real geometric clip (clip GLB to bbox, or use OSM2World `--tile` mode which clips) for production. (4) Mesh is many small meshes (~3700) — merge by material for three.js draw-call perf.

**Test artifacts (git-ignored, untracked):** `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/` has `eiffel.osm` (over-broad), `eiffel2.osm` (clipped via `node(w)`), `eiffel_lod{0,1,2}.glb`, preview PNGs. Headless previewer: `scripts/preview-osm2world.mjs <relpath.glb>` (puppeteer + three r128 + GLTFLoader 0.128; flags `--use-gl=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`; prints tris/meshes/materials/bbox, writes `_preview_persp/top.png`). The 193MB LOD4 GLBs were deleted (regenerable).

**Status:** Evaluation done AND a first **Paris GP** world is INTEGRATED + verified in-game (2026-06-18). Pipeline now: `eiffel_lod2.glb` → `scripts/build-paris-world.mjs` (puppeteer + GLTFLoader/GLTFExporter r128/0.128: per-triangle clip to a ±340m square around the median centre + vertical band `[ground-25, ground+360]` to kill the comet-tails AND a stray 657m spike / sub-ground object; recentre to origin with ground→y=0; bake material+vertex colours into ONE per-vertex-coloured mesh) → **`assets/paris/world.glb`** (98k tris, ~10MB, Eiffel ~330m tall, tower at ~(-45,-82) in world coords).

Integrated in `index.html` exactly like [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]]: `buildParisWorld()` (loads world.glb, reassigns `MeshLambertMaterial{vertexColors:true}`, hides the generic 900² `groundMesh`, adds a base plane at y=-0.6), a `'paris'` branch in `buildWorld` (uses a VISIBLE `buildTrackMeshes` ribbon over the city, unlike Mishkenot), `PARIS_CTRL` (provisional oval looping AROUND the tower), `VTHEME.paris`, a PARIS GP button (`startParis`, class `.paris`), `?world=paris` deep-link. Verify with `scripts/verify-paris.mjs` (writes `assets/paris/_ingame_{overview,top,live}.png`). Confirmed: tower stands, karts spawn on the grid, drivable.

**Next (user's call):** route `PARIS_CTRL` onto the REAL avenues instead of the provisional oval (track currently clips through some footprints); optionally tighten clip slivers; recolor pass if a more stylised palette is wanted. Keep [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (karts stay voxel).

**Mishkenot rebuilt via OSM2World (2026-06-18) — supersedes the 3MF approach in [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]].** Adds two reusable techniques:
- **Area picker** `scripts/area-picker.mjs`: a Leaflet (satellite+street) map server on :8765 where the USER click-draws a polygon (click first point to close) → POSTs `{polygon:[[lat,lon]...], bbox, center}` to `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/area.json`. This is how the user hands over an exact area.
- **Exact-polygon clip with deterministic projection:** OSM2World's default `MetricMapProjection` origin = centre of the data's lat/lon bounds, and `OSMData` prefers an explicit `<bounds>` element over node min/max. So: download bbox (polygon bbox + ~0.0005° margin) via the `node(w)` Overpass query, **inject `<bounds>` = that bbox into the .osm** (origin becomes the bbox CENTRE, deterministic), convert LOD2. Then `scripts/build-mishkenot-world.mjs` projects the polygon to GLB XZ with the SAME projection — `scale=40075016.686*cos(originLat)`, `X=(lon-originLon)/360*scale`, `Z=-(latToY(lat)-latToY(originLat))*scale` (GltfOutput negates z; `latToY=ln((1+sin)/(1-sin))/(4π)+0.5`), origin=`area.json` bbox centre — and clips triangles by **point-in-polygon** on centroids (+ vertical band `[gy-25, gy+140]`), recentres on the projected-polygon bbox centre, bakes colours, exports `assets/mishkenot/world.glb` (~96k tris, 9.9MB, footprint ~1323×1256m, low-rise ≤75m). Verified in-game (top-down matches the drawn polygon exactly). Game integration is identical to Paris (`buildMishkenotWorld` loads the GLB, visible `buildTrackMeshes` ribbon, `MISHKENOT_CTRL` resized to ~±380/330). Old 3MF assets (`world.bin`/`buildings.glb`/`world.json`) deleted.

I dug into both the repo and your area's data, and here's the honest answer.

**Not *exactly* — and here's why.** OSM2World builds models from OpenStreetMap **tags**, not from photos or 3D scans, so it fundamentally can't reproduce the real facades of specific buildings. Two hard limits for your area specifically:

1. **The OSM data is sparse.** Of the **538 buildings** in your polygon, only **16** have a floor count, **11** have a height, **5** have a roof shape, and **0** have any colour, material, or roof tags. So OSM2World has almost nothing to work with and falls back to identical default boxes — that's the uniform olive look you see.
2. **The realistic textures aren't in this repo.** The nice brick/plaster/window renders on osm2world.org come from a separate texture pack; this clone ships only test images (`test.png`, `glass.png`). With the default config it can only output flat colors — which is exactly what we got.

**What I *can* do to make it read like the real neighborhood** (all using what we have, no photoreal claim):
- **Vary heights** — use the real heights/levels where tagged, estimate the rest from footprint size, so it's not one flat height.
- **Realistic palette** — sandy/cream/white walls + terracotta/grey roofs, varied per building (very Mediterranean/Israeli residential), instead of uniform olive.
- Keep it flat/low-poly so it still matches your voxel karts.

There's also a heavier route (wire in a generic texture pack) and a "truly accurate" route (manually tag all ~500 buildings' heights/colors in OSM — impractical). Let me check which direction you want:

The editor is rebuilt and live (page + Street View proxy both responding).

### 👉 Open it: **http://localhost:8767/**

You'll see Mishkenot from above with all **301 building footprints** outlined. Here's the workflow:

1. **Click a building** → its panel opens with the building's **real Street View photo** (use **◀ look / look ▶** to rotate the camera around it if the first angle is blocked by trees).
2. **Pick a type** based on what you see in the photo:
   - **A — Apartment block** (white, flat roof, 4 storeys)
   - **B — Villa, flat roof** (cream, 2 storeys)
   - **C — Villa, tiled roof** (cream + red tiles, 2 storeys)
3. Adjust **storeys** if it's taller/shorter than the preset, then hit **set**.
4. Assigned buildings fill in with their type color (blue/orange/red); unset ones stay outlined — so you can see your progress (the `(x/301)` counter at the top).

**Tips to make 301 manageable:**

name: osm2world-world-pipeline
description: "OSM2World (vendored Java repo) evaluated as a from-OSM world-geometry generator for AniRacers — build + convert recipe, LOD sizes, gotchas"
metadata:

OSM2World (`OSM2World/`, MIT, Java/Maven, v0.5.0-SNAPSHOT) was vendored and evaluated on 2026-06-18 as a candidate generator for AniRacers race worlds, using the **Eiffel Tower / Champ de Mars** area as a test. Verdict: **viable and lower-effort than the hand-built [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]] or the [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]] mesh-wrangling** — it auto-produces a recognizable real place. Outputs **GLB that is Y-up, real metres, `(x,y,-z)`** → drops straight into the game's existing GLTFLoader path (same as Mishkenot), no axis rotation.

**Build (one-time, env-specific):** Maven was NOT installed (only JDK present). Downloaded Maven 3.9.9 zip to `C:\Users\YonatanSetbon\tools\apache-maven-3.9.9\`. Build with **JDK 17** (`C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17`, the project's target; JDK 14/17/24 all present). The CLI lives in the `desktop` module; build only what's needed and skip the slow/fragile bits: `mvn -f OSM2World/pom.xml -pl desktop -am -DskipTests -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true package` (run via PowerShell `--%` stop-parsing or the `-D` args get mangled). Skipping `-am`'s `core-web` (TeaVM Java→JS) module avoids a long, fragile step. Output: `OSM2World/desktop/target/osm2world-desktop-0.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` + `target/lib/` (121 jars; manifest Class-Path already wired). Main class `org.osm2world.console.OSM2World`.

**Convert:** `java [--add-exports java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED ...] -jar <jar> convert -i <in.osm> -o <out.glb> --lod 0..4`. Reads an OSM file or live Overpass (`--input_mode OVERPASS`); `convert` always requires `-i` so file input is simplest. Default config emits **flat-shaded solid-color geometry, only ~2 materials, NO textures** — boxy extruded buildings with real roof shapes = reads as blocky/low-poly, compatible-ish with the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (recolor the 2 materials to the palette; karts/animals stay voxel).

**LOD is the cost knob (Eiffel ~700m bbox):** LOD4 = 1.82M tris / **193 MB** (too heavy for web — every tree a 3D model, full Eiffel lattice, facade detail); **LOD2 = 128k tris / 18 MB** (visually ~identical at gameplay distance, the keeper); LOD1/LOD0 ≈ 12 MB. Convert ≈ 20–30s. Game already runs the ~761k-tri Mishkenot world, so LOD2 is light.

**Gotchas:** (1) `OSMFileReader` is a record that does NOT override `getData(LatLonBounds)` → **`--input_bbox` is ignored for file input**; you must bound at the Overpass query. (2) `way(bbox)`/`>;` recursion drags in city-wide route/river **relation** members (first try = 10km extent, 183MB). Use `node(w)` recursion not `>;`, and drop or non-recurse relations. (3) Even then, complete ways crossing the bbox edge leave "comet-tail" line artifacts beyond the area — needs a real geometric clip (clip GLB to bbox, or use OSM2World `--tile` mode which clips) for production. (4) Mesh is many small meshes (~3700) — merge by material for three.js draw-call perf.

**Test artifacts (git-ignored, untracked):** `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/` has `eiffel.osm` (over-broad), `eiffel2.osm` (clipped via `node(w)`), `eiffel_lod{0,1,2}.glb`, preview PNGs. Headless previewer: `scripts/preview-osm2world.mjs <relpath.glb>` (puppeteer + three r128 + GLTFLoader 0.128; flags `--use-gl=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`; prints tris/meshes/materials/bbox, writes `_preview_persp/top.png`). The 193MB LOD4 GLBs were deleted (regenerable).

---
name: osm2world-world-pipeline
description: "OSM2World (vendored Java repo) evaluated as a from-OSM world-geometry generator for AniRacers — build + convert recipe, LOD sizes, gotchas"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d45cbd15-7c08-4d07-9f7e-9203188d7f9f
---

OSM2World (`OSM2World/`, MIT, Java/Maven, v0.5.0-SNAPSHOT) was vendored and evaluated on 2026-06-18 as a candidate generator for AniRacers race worlds, using the **Eiffel Tower / Champ de Mars** area as a test. Verdict: **viable and lower-effort than the hand-built [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]] or the [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]] mesh-wrangling** — it auto-produces a recognizable real place. Outputs **GLB that is Y-up, real metres, `(x,y,-z)`** → drops straight into the game's existing GLTFLoader path (same as Mishkenot), no axis rotation.

**Build (one-time, env-specific):** Maven was NOT installed (only JDK present). Downloaded Maven 3.9.9 zip to `C:\Users\YonatanSetbon\tools\apache-maven-3.9.9\`. Build with **JDK 17** (`C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17`, the project's target; JDK 14/17/24 all present). The CLI lives in the `desktop` module; build only what's needed and skip the slow/fragile bits: `mvn -f OSM2World/pom.xml -pl desktop -am -DskipTests -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true package` (run via PowerShell `--%` stop-parsing or the `-D` args get mangled). Skipping `-am`'s `core-web` (TeaVM Java→JS) module avoids a long, fragile step. Output: `OSM2World/desktop/target/osm2world-desktop-0.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` + `target/lib/` (121 jars; manifest Class-Path already wired). Main class `org.osm2world.console.OSM2World`.

**Convert:** `java [--add-exports java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED ...] -jar <jar> convert -i <in.osm> -o <out.glb> --lod 0..4`. Reads an OSM file or live Overpass (`--input_mode OVERPASS`); `convert` always requires `-i` so file input is simplest. Default config emits **flat-shaded solid-color geometry, only ~2 materials, NO textures** — boxy extruded buildings with real roof shapes = reads as blocky/low-poly, compatible-ish with the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (recolor the 2 materials to the palette; karts/animals stay voxel).

**LOD is the cost knob (Eiffel ~700m bbox):** LOD4 = 1.82M tris / **193 MB** (too heavy for web — every tree a 3D model, full Eiffel lattice, facade detail); **LOD2 = 128k tris / 18 MB** (visually ~identical at gameplay distance, the keeper); LOD1/LOD0 ≈ 12 MB. Convert ≈ 20–30s. Game already runs the ~761k-tri Mishkenot world, so LOD2 is light.

**Gotchas:** (1) `OSMFileReader` is a record that does NOT override `getData(LatLonBounds)` → **`--input_bbox` is ignored for file input**; you must bound at the Overpass query. (2) `way(bbox)`/`>;` recursion drags in city-wide route/river **relation** members (first try = 10km extent, 183MB). Use `node(w)` recursion not `>;`, and drop or non-recurse relations. (3) Even then, complete ways crossing the bbox edge leave "comet-tail" line artifacts beyond the area — needs a real geometric clip (clip GLB to bbox, or use OSM2World `--tile` mode which clips) for production. (4) Mesh is many small meshes (~3700) — merge by material for three.js draw-call perf.

**Test artifacts (git-ignored, untracked):** `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/` has `eiffel.osm` (over-broad), `eiffel2.osm` (clipped via `node(w)`), `eiffel_lod{0,1,2}.glb`, preview PNGs. Headless previewer: `scripts/preview-osm2world.mjs <relpath.glb>` (puppeteer + three r128 + GLTFLoader 0.128; flags `--use-gl=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`; prints tris/meshes/materials/bbox, writes `_preview_persp/top.png`). The 193MB LOD4 GLBs were deleted (regenerable).

**Status:** Evaluation done AND a first **Paris GP** world is INTEGRATED + verified in-game (2026-06-18). Pipeline now: `eiffel_lod2.glb` → `scripts/build-paris-world.mjs` (puppeteer + GLTFLoader/GLTFExporter r128/0.128: per-triangle clip to a ±340m square around the median centre + vertical band `[ground-25, ground+360]` to kill the comet-tails AND a stray 657m spike / sub-ground object; recentre to origin with ground→y=0; bake material+vertex colours into ONE per-vertex-coloured mesh) → **`assets/paris/world.glb`** (98k tris, ~10MB, Eiffel ~330m tall, tower at ~(-45,-82) in world coords).

Integrated in `index.html` exactly like [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]]: `buildParisWorld()` (loads world.glb, reassigns `MeshLambertMaterial{vertexColors:true}`, hides the generic 900² `groundMesh`, adds a base plane at y=-0.6), a `'paris'` branch in `buildWorld` (uses a VISIBLE `buildTrackMeshes` ribbon over the city, unlike Mishkenot), `PARIS_CTRL` (provisional oval looping AROUND the tower), `VTHEME.paris`, a PARIS GP button (`startParis`, class `.paris`), `?world=paris` deep-link. Verify with `scripts/verify-paris.mjs` (writes `assets/paris/_ingame_{overview,top,live}.png`). Confirmed: tower stands, karts spawn on the grid, drivable.

**Next (user's call):** route `PARIS_CTRL` onto the REAL avenues instead of the provisional oval (track currently clips through some footprints); optionally tighten clip slivers; recolor pass if a more stylised palette is wanted. Keep [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (karts stay voxel).

**Mishkenot rebuilt via OSM2World (2026-06-18) — supersedes the 3MF approach in [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]].** Adds two reusable techniques:
- **Area picker** `scripts/area-picker.mjs`: a Leaflet (satellite+street) map server on :8765 where the USER click-draws a polygon (click first point to close) → POSTs `{polygon:[[lat,lon]...], bbox, center}` to `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/area.json`. This is how the user hands over an exact area.
- **Exact-polygon clip with deterministic projection:** OSM2World's default `MetricMapProjection` origin = centre of the data's lat/lon bounds, and `OSMData` prefers an explicit `<bounds>` element over node min/max. So: download bbox (polygon bbox + ~0.0005° margin) via the `node(w)` Overpass query, **inject `<bounds>` = that bbox into the .osm** (origin becomes the bbox CENTRE, deterministic), convert LOD2. Then `scripts/build-mishkenot-world.mjs` projects the polygon to GLB XZ with the SAME projection — `scale=40075016.686*cos(originLat)`, `X=(lon-originLon)/360*scale`, `Z=-(latToY(lat)-latToY(originLat))*scale` (GltfOutput negates z; `latToY=ln((1+sin)/(1-sin))/(4π)+0.5`), origin=`area.json` bbox centre — and clips triangles by **point-in-polygon** on centroids (+ vertical band `[gy-25, gy+140]`), recentres on the projected-polygon bbox centre, bakes colours, exports `assets/mishkenot/world.glb` (~96k tris, 9.9MB, footprint ~1323×1256m, low-rise ≤75m). Verified in-game (top-down matches the drawn polygon exactly). Game integration is identical to Paris (`buildMishkenotWorld` loads the GLB, visible `buildTrackMeshes` ribbon). Old 3MF assets (`world.bin`/`buildings.glb`/`world.json`) deleted.

**Per-building realism via Street View (2026-06-18).** OSM2World only renders what OSM tags say, and this area's data is sparse (538 buildings, ~16 with levels, 0 with colour/roof). So: read the real houses from Google Street View (key in `.env` `GMAPS_KEY`, Street View Static), classify each building into a few types, write those back as OSM tags, re-run OSM2World. Tools:
- `scripts/mishkenot-streetview.mjs` — samples SV along the track (inverse-projects world XZ→lat/lon) to characterise the area. Mishkenot = white/cream **apartment blocks (4–5 floors, flat roof)** + **villas (1–2 floors, mostly flat, some red-tiled)**, lots of eucalyptus parkland.
- `scripts/extract-buildings.mjs` → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/buildings.json`: every building way inside the polygon as footprint+centroid in world XZ (SAME projection: toXZ minus PCX/PCZ) + lat/lon + area. (301 buildings inside the polygon.)
- `scripts/building-editor.mjs` (server :8767, run with `--env-file=.env`): top-down world + clickable footprints; clicking a building shows its **real Street View photo** (`/sv?id=` proxy: nearest pano via metadata API, heading=bearing→centroid, cached to streetview/bld_*.jpg), set type A/B/C + storeys, "Auto-fill by size", Save → `building-overrides.json`.
- `scripts/apply-building-overrides.mjs`: injects `building:levels`/`height`(=lv*3.2)/`building:colour`/`roof:shape`/`roof:colour` per building way into `mishkenot_tagged.osm` (TYPES preset: A white #eef0f2 flat, B cream #f0e7d4 flat, C cream+#b6523a gabled; strips pre-existing dup tags; KEEPS `<bounds>`), then re-run OSM2World convert (→ mishkenot_osm.glb) + build-mishkenot-world. Result (current): 301 buildings tagged (126 A / 175 B), buildings now cream/white at 2–4 storeys, max height 19.8m — verified in-game, matches the real neighbourhood character. Honest ceiling: matches CHARACTER (colour/height/roof), not photo-exact facades.

---
name: osm2world-world-pipeline
description: "OSM2World (vendored Java repo) evaluated as a from-OSM world-geometry generator for AniRacers — build + convert recipe, LOD sizes, gotchas"
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: project
  originSessionId: d45cbd15-7c08-4d07-9f7e-9203188d7f9f
---

OSM2World (`OSM2World/`, MIT, Java/Maven, v0.5.0-SNAPSHOT) was vendored and evaluated on 2026-06-18 as a candidate generator for AniRacers race worlds, using the **Eiffel Tower / Champ de Mars** area as a test. Verdict: **viable and lower-effort than the hand-built [[sarcelles-world-pipeline]] or the [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]] mesh-wrangling** — it auto-produces a recognizable real place. Outputs **GLB that is Y-up, real metres, `(x,y,-z)`** → drops straight into the game's existing GLTFLoader path (same as Mishkenot), no axis rotation.

**Build (one-time, env-specific):** Maven was NOT installed (only JDK present). Downloaded Maven 3.9.9 zip to `C:\Users\YonatanSetbon\tools\apache-maven-3.9.9\`. Build with **JDK 17** (`C:\Program Files\Java\jdk-17`, the project's target; JDK 14/17/24 all present). The CLI lives in the `desktop` module; build only what's needed and skip the slow/fragile bits: `mvn -f OSM2World/pom.xml -pl desktop -am -DskipTests -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true package` (run via PowerShell `--%` stop-parsing or the `-D` args get mangled). Skipping `-am`'s `core-web` (TeaVM Java→JS) module avoids a long, fragile step. Output: `OSM2World/desktop/target/osm2world-desktop-0.5.0-SNAPSHOT.jar` + `target/lib/` (121 jars; manifest Class-Path already wired). Main class `org.osm2world.console.OSM2World`.

**Convert:** `java [--add-exports java.base/java.lang=ALL-UNNAMED ...] -jar <jar> convert -i <in.osm> -o <out.glb> --lod 0..4`. Reads an OSM file or live Overpass (`--input_mode OVERPASS`); `convert` always requires `-i` so file input is simplest. Default config emits **flat-shaded solid-color geometry, only ~2 materials, NO textures** — boxy extruded buildings with real roof shapes = reads as blocky/low-poly, compatible-ish with the [[aniracers-block-aesthetic]] (recolor the 2 materials to the palette; karts/animals stay voxel).

**LOD is the cost knob (Eiffel ~700m bbox):** LOD4 = 1.82M tris / **193 MB** (too heavy for web — every tree a 3D model, full Eiffel lattice, facade detail); **LOD2 = 128k tris / 18 MB** (visually ~identical at gameplay distance, the keeper); LOD1/LOD0 ≈ 12 MB. Convert ≈ 20–30s. Game already runs the ~761k-tri Mishkenot world, so LOD2 is light.

**Gotchas:** (1) `OSMFileReader` is a record that does NOT override `getData(LatLonBounds)` → **`--input_bbox` is ignored for file input**; you must bound at the Overpass query. (2) `way(bbox)`/`>;` recursion drags in city-wide route/river **relation** members (first try = 10km extent, 183MB). Use `node(w)` recursion not `>;`, and drop or non-recurse relations. (3) Even then, complete ways crossing the bbox edge leave "comet-tail" line artifacts beyond the area — needs a real geometric clip (clip GLB to bbox, or use OSM2World `--tile` mode which clips) for production. (4) Mesh is many small meshes (~3700) — merge by material for three.js draw-call perf.

**Test artifacts (git-ignored, untracked):** `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/` has `eiffel.osm` (over-broad), `eiffel2.osm` (clipped via `node(w)`), `eiffel_lod{0,1,2}.glb`, preview PNGs. Headless previewer: `scripts/preview-osm2world.mjs <relpath.glb>` (puppeteer + three r128 + GLTFLoader 0.128; flags `--use-gl=swiftshader --enable-unsafe-swiftshader`; prints tris/meshes/materials/bbox, writes `_preview_persp/top.png`). The 193MB LOD4 GLBs were deleted (regenerable).

**Status:** Evaluation done AND a first **Paris GP** world is INTEGRATED + verified in-game (2026-06-18). Pipeline now: `eiffel_lod2.glb` → `scripts/build-paris-world.mjs` (puppeteer + GLTFLoader/GLTFExporter r128/0.128: per-triangle clip to a ±340m square around the median centre + vertical band `[ground-25, ground+360]` to kill the comet-tails AND a stray 657m spike / sub-ground object; recentre to origin with ground→y=0; bake material+vertex colours into ONE per-vertex-coloured mesh) → **`assets/paris/world.glb`** (98k tris, ~10MB, Eiffel ~330m tall, tower at ~(-45,-82) in world coords).

Integrated in `index.html` exactly like [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]]: `buildParisWorld()` (loads world.glb, reassigns `MeshLambertMaterial{vertexColors:true}`, hides the generic 900² `groundMesh`, adds a base plane at y=-0.6), a `'paris'` branch in `buildWorld` (uses a VISIBLE `buildTrackMeshes` ribbon over the city, unlike Mishkenot), `PARIS_CTRL` (provisional oval looping AROUND the tower), `VTHEME.paris`, a PARIS GP button (`startParis`, class `.paris`), `?world=paris` deep-link. **Mishkenot rebuilt via OSM2World (2026-06-18) — supersedes the 3MF approach in [[mishkenot-zvulun-3mf-world]].** Adds two reusable techniques:
- **Area picker** `scripts/area-picker.mjs`: a Leaflet (satellite+street) map server on :8765 where the USER click-draws a polygon (click first point to close) → POSTs `{polygon:[[lat,lon]...], bbox, center}` to `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/area.json`. This is how the user hands over an exact area.
- **Exact-polygon clip with deterministic projection:** OSM2World's default `MetricMapProjection` origin = centre of the data's lat/lon bounds, and `OSMData` prefers an explicit `<bounds>` element over node min/max. So: download bbox (polygon bbox + ~0.0005° margin) via the `node(w)` Overpass query, **inject `<bounds>` = that bbox into the .osm** (origin becomes the bbox CENTRE, deterministic), convert LOD2. Then `scripts/build-mishkenot-world.mjs` projects the polygon to GLB XZ with the SAME projection — `scale=40075016.686*cos(originLat)`, `X=(lon-originLon)/360*scale`, `Z=-(latToY(lat)-latToY(originLat))*scale` (GltfOutput negates z; `latToY=ln((1+sin)/(1-sin))/(4π)+0.5`), origin=`area.json` bbox centre — and clips triangles by **point-in-polygon** on centroids (+ vertical band `[gy-25, gy+140]`), recentres on the projected-polygon bbox centre, bakes colours, exports `assets/mishkenot/world.glb` (~96k tris, 9.9MB, footprint ~1323×1256m, low-rise ≤75m). Old 3MF assets (`world.bin`/`buildings.glb`/`world.json`) deleted.

**Per-building realism via Street View (2026-06-18).** OSM2World only renders what OSM tags say, and this area's data is sparse (538 buildings, ~16 with levels, 0 with colour/roof). - `scripts/extract-buildings.mjs` → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/buildings.json`: every building way inside the polygon as footprint+centroid in world XZ (SAME projection: toXZ minus PCX/PCZ) + lat/lon + area. (301 buildings inside the polygon.)
- `scripts/building-editor.mjs` (server :8767, run with `--env-file=.env`): top-down world + clickable footprints; clicking a building shows its **real Street View photo** (`/sv?id=` proxy: nearest pano via metadata API, heading=bearing→centroid, cached to streetview/bld_*.jpg), set type A/B/C + storeys, "Auto-fill by size", Save → `building-overrides.json`.

Result (current): 301 buildings tagged (126 A / 175 B), buildings now cream/white at 2–4 storeys, max height 19.8m — verified in-game, matches the real neighbourhood character. Honest ceiling: matches CHARACTER (colour/height/roof), not photo-exact facades.

**Custom 3D house models instanced per footprint (2026-06-18).** The user wanted buildings to actually LOOK like the real houses, not OSM2World's flat extrusions. So the 3 types are now hand-built voxel/box models (matching the karts), defined+previewed in `scripts/building-types-viewer.mjs` (server :8768, OrbitControls + live sliders): **A** apartment block (white, balconies, rooftop dud/solar), **B** semi-detached **cottage** (two units sharing a central wall, 2 doors, cream+stone base, flat roof w/ overhang — user-specified, ref `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/option B.png`), **C** villa w/ red hipped tiled roof. The same `makeBuilding()` factory is used to INSTANCE a model onto each footprint: `scripts/strip-buildings-osm.mjs` (removes building/roof/height tags → base streets/parks/trees) → convert `mishkenot_base.glb` → `scripts/build-mishkenot-instanced.mjs` (puppeteer: clip base to polygon, then for each building compute an OBB from its footprint (longest-edge orientation θ, width/depth spans, centre), build the A/B/C model sized W×D×floors, `rotation.y=-θ`, position at footprint centre, bake all colours to one vertex-coloured mesh, export). To re-run after editing types/assignments: strip+convert base (once) → `node scripts/build-mishkenot-instanced.mjs`.

# Building photo → 3D model spec

You are analyzing Google Street View photos of buildings in the **Mishkenot Zvulun / Nof HaTalmim** neighborhood of **Netanya, Israel**, to produce a 3D-model spec for each building in a low-poly racing game.

## Input
You will be told a chunk file path and an output file path. Read the chunk JSON: it is an array of buildings, each `{id, img, area, levels, dist, conf}` where `img` is the absolute path to the photo, `area` is footprint m² (may be null), `levels` is the OSM floor count (may be null), `dist` is metres from camera.

For **each** building, use the **Read** tool on `img` to view the photo, then decide its spec. The camera is aimed at the building's centroid — focus on the most prominent building near the **center** of the frame. Photos may be partly blocked by trees/walls/cars or show several buildings; do your best and lower `conf` when unsure.

## Output spec — EXACTLY these fields per building
- `floors`: integer 1–25. **If `levels` is given, use it** (authoritative) unless the photo flatly contradicts it. If `levels` is null, estimate from window rows; fall back to: area>250 → 4, else 2.
- `wall`: hex `"#rrggbb"` of the dominant wall colour. Realistic Israeli-residential tones — white `#f2f0ea`, cream `#ece3d0`, beige `#e6d8bd`, light grey `#dfe1e3`, sandstone `#d8cdb5`, ochre `#e3c98f`. Pick the closest (or a nearby hex).

- `roofColor`: hex. Flat ≈ `"#c9cdd2"` (grey). Tiled ≈ `"#b25a3c"` (terracotta).

# Building photo → 3D model spec

You are analyzing Google Street View photos of buildings in the **Mishkenot Zvulun / Nof HaTalmim** neighborhood of **Netanya, Israel**, to produce a 3D-model spec for each building in a low-poly racing game.

## Input
You will be told a chunk file path and an output file path. Read the chunk JSON: it is an array of buildings, each `{id, img, area, levels, dist, conf}` where `img` is the absolute path to the photo, `area` is footprint m² (may be null), `levels` is the OSM floor count (may be null), `dist` is metres from camera.

For **each** building, use the **Read** tool on `img` to view the photo, then decide its spec. The camera is aimed at the building's centroid — focus on the most prominent building near the **center** of the frame. Photos may be partly blocked by trees/walls/cars or show several buildings; do your best and lower `conf` when unsure.

## Output spec — EXACTLY these fields per building
- `floors`: integer 1–25. **If `levels` is given, use it** (authoritative) unless the photo flatly contradicts it. If `levels` is null, estimate from window rows; fall back to: area>250 → 4, else 2.
- `wall`: hex `"#rrggbb"` of the dominant wall colour. Realistic Israeli-residential tones — white `#f2f0ea`, cream `#ece3d0`, beige `#e6d8bd`, light grey `#dfe1e3`, sandstone `#d8cdb5`, ochre `#e3c98f`. Pick the closest (or a nearby hex).
- `roof`: `"flat"` | `"gabled"` | `"hipped"`. Most apartment blocks/towers and many houses are `"flat"`. Red/orange tiled pitched roofs → `"gabled"` (long ridge) or `"hipped"` (4-sided pyramid).
- `roofColor`: hex. Flat ≈ `"#c9cdd2"` (grey). Tiled ≈ `"#b25a3c"` (terracotta).
- `cols`: integer 1–8 = windows per floor across the visible facade width. Towers/blocks 4–6, houses 2–3.
- `balconies`: true if the facade has rows of protruding balconies (typical of apartment blocks/towers); else false.
- `doors`: 2 if clearly a semi-detached pair (two front doors / mirrored houses); else 1.
- `shutters`: true if windows have prominent external shutters/blinds (common on houses); else false.
- `stoneBase`: true if the ground floor/base is clad in stone or a different material from the upper walls; else false.
- `solar`: true if rooftop solar water heaters (white/black cylinders + panels) or rooftop water tanks are visible; else false.
- `style`: `"tower"` (≥8 floors) | `"apartment"` (4–7) | `"house"` (1–3 low/detached) | `"villa"` (1–3 with tiled roof).
- `conf`: `"high"` | `"med"` | `"low"` — how clearly the photo shows THIS building.
- `notes`: ≤8 words.

When the photo is unusable (only trees/wall/sky/road, or clearly a far different building), set `conf:"low"` and choose sensible defaults from area/levels (big+tall → tower/apartment, flat roof, balconies; small → house, flat or tiled roof).

## Write the result
Use the **Write** tool to write the output file path as strict JSON, no prose:
```
{"chunk":<k>,"specs":{"<id>":{ ...spec... }, ...}}
```
Then reply with ONE line only: `chunk <k>: N specs, <#high>/<#med>/<#low> conf`.

Pipeline is in motion. Here's where things stand:

**Done**
- ✅ **Harvested 300/301 Street View photos** — one per building, framed on each footprint (nearest pano ~25–40m, FOV auto-zoomed by distance). Manifest records pano distance + confidence.
- ✅ **Wrote a spec-driven model factory** (`build-mishkenot-from-specs.mjs`) — each building is now built from its own params: floors, wall colour, roof shape (flat/gabled/hipped), window-grid density, balconies, 1-or-2 doors, shutters, stone base, rooftop solar. A/B/C presets remain the fallback.
- ✅ **Wrote the merge step** ready to assemble the specs.

**Running now**
- 🔄 **15 vision agents** analyzing all 300 photos in parallel (20 each), each writing a per-building spec. I'll merge them into `building-specs.json` as they finish.

One thing the photos already told me: this area isn't cottages — it's mostly **real Netanya apartment towers** (OSM says up to 17 floors) with stone/white cladding and balconies, mixed with 1–2 storey flat-roof houses (rooftop solar tanks everywhere) and some red-tile-roof villas. Going photo-by-photo is exactly right — the old "cream cottage" look was wrong for most of the map.

I'll report back with the spec distribution and the rebuilt world once the agents land and I bake it.

aiTitle: Explore osm2world and build Paris Eiffel Tower demo

content.text:
The world looks great in-game — the kart now races down a real street: cream/white 2-storey houses with windows, doors and shutters on both sides, apartment blocks, red-tile villas in the distance, and the tall towers standing further back. Every building is now its own photo-derived model.

Now to your request — a gallery of **all buildings in a row**, like the :8768 type viewer but for all 300. I'll first extract the house factory into a shared file (so the gallery and the world-builder always render identically), then build the gallery with each model next to its real Street View photo for comparison.

<script>
window.RESULT=null;window.ERR=null;
var POLY=`+JSON.stringify(POLY)+`, PCX=`+PCX+`, PCZ=`+PCZ+`, BUILD=`+JSON.stringify(BUILDINGS)+`;
var FLOOR_H=3.0;
function hx(c){return (typeof c==='number')?c:new THREE.Color(c).getHex();}
function box(w,h,d,color,x,y,z){var m=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.BoxGeometry(Math.max(0.02,w),Math.max(0.02,h),Math.max(0.02,d)),new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({color:hx(color)}));m.position.set(x,y,z);return m;}

// ---- windows on all four facades; cols across width, colD across depth ----
function addWindows(g,W,H,D,floors,glass,cols,shutters,doors){
  cols=Math.max(1,cols||Math.max(2,Math.round(W/3.4)));
  var colD=Math.max(1,Math.round(D/3.6));
  var winW=Math.min(1.4,(W/cols)*0.55),winH=1.45,winD=Math.min(1.4,(D/colD)*0.55);
  var doorXs=doors>=2?[-W/4,W/4]:[0];
  for(var f=0;f<floors;f++){var y=f*FLOOR_H+FLOOR_H*0.55;
    for(var c=0;c<cols;c++){var x=-W/2+(c+0.5)*(W/cols);
      var nearDoor=false;for(var di=0;di<doorXs.length;di++)if(Math.abs(x-doorXs[di])<1.2)nearDoor=true;
      if(f===0&&nearDoor)continue;
      g.add(box(winW,winH,0.14,glass,x,y,D/2+0.02));g.add(box(winW,winH,0.14,glass,x,y,-D/2-0.02));
      if(shutters){g.add(box(winW+0.22,winH+0.1,0.06,0xb7ad97,x,y,D/2+0.05));}}
    for(var k=0;k<colD;k++){var z=-D/2+(k+0.5)*(D/colD);
      g.add(box(0.14,winH,winD,glass,W/2+0.02,y,z));g.add(box(0.14,winH,winD,glass,-W/2-0.02,y,z));}}
}
function addBalconies(g,W,H,D,floors){for(var f=1;f<floors;f++){var y=f*FLOOR_H;
  g.add(box(W*0.84,0.18,1.1,0xe4e1d8,0,y+0.05,D/2+0.55));g.add(box(W*0.84,0.7,0.1,0xf3f1ea,0,y+0.45,D/2+1.05));
  for(var x=-W*0.4;x<=W*0.4;x+=1.1)g.add(box(0.08,0.7,0.08,0xf3f1ea,x,y+0.45,D/2+1.05));}}
function addDoors(g,W,D,doors){var xs=doors>=2?[-W/4,W/4]:[0];
  for(var i=0;i<xs.length;i++){g.add(box(1.25,2.25,0.16,0x5a4636,xs[i],1.12,D/2+0.06));
    g.add(box(1.7,0.16,0.9,0xf0ede4,xs[i],2.4,D/2+0.42));}}  // small canopy over each door
// ---- roofs ----
function addFlatRoof(g,W,H,D,roof,solar){g.add(box(W+0.2,0.25,D+0.2,roof,0,H+0.12,0));
  var E=[[0,D/2],[0,-D/2],[W/2,0],[-W/2,0]];for(var i=0;i<4;i++){var hz=E[i][1]!==0;g.add(box(hz?W+0.3:0.25,0.5,hz?0.25:D+0.3,0xe7e7e7,E[i][0],H+0.45,E[i][1]));}
  if(solar){g.add(new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.CylinderGeometry(0.5,0.5,2.2,12),new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({color:0xf2f2f2})).translateX(-W*0.2).translateY(H+1.3).translateZ(-D*0.15));
    var p=box(2.6,0.12,1.4,0x24405e,W*0.18,H+0.9,D*0.05);p.rotation.x=-0.5;g.add(p);g.add(box(0.6,0.6,0.6,0x333333,W*0.18,H+0.5,D*0.05));}}
function gablePrism(W,D,rh,color){ // ridge along the LONGER horizontal axis
  var alongX=W>=D, L=alongX?W:D, S=alongX?D:W; var hl=L/2,hs=S/2;
  // cross-section apex at top; build 4 faces as triangles in local (ridge along X) then rotate if needed
  var A=[-hl,0,-hs],B=[hl,0,-hs],C=[hl,0,hs],E=[-hl,0,hs],R0=[-hl,rh,0],R1=[hl,rh,0];
  var tris=[A,B,R1, A,R1,R0,  E,R0,R1, E,R1,C,  A,R0,E,  B,C,R1];
  var pos=[];for(var i=0;i<tris.length;i++){var v=tris[i];if(!alongX){var t=v[0];v=[v[2],v[1],-t];}pos.push(v[0],v[1],v[2]);}
  var geo=new THREE.BufferGeometry();geo.setAttribute('position',new THREE.Float32BufferAttribute(pos,3));geo.computeVertexNormals();
  return new THREE.Mesh(geo,new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({color:hx(color),side:THREE.DoubleSide}));}
function addGableRoof(g,W,H,D,roof){var rh=Math.max(1.8,Math.min(W,D)*0.42);
  g.add(box(W+0.6,0.2,D+0.6,0x8a7e6a,0,H+0.1,0));var m=gablePrism(W+0.6,D+0.6,rh,roof);m.position.y=H+0.18;g.add(m);}
function addHipRoof(g,W,H,D,roof){var rh=Math.max(2.0,Math.min(W,D)*0.36);
  var c=new THREE.Mesh(new THREE.ConeGeometry(Math.SQRT2/2,1,4),new THREE.MeshLambertMaterial({color:hx(roof)}));
  c.scale.set(W+1.0,rh,D+1.0);c.rotation.y=Math.PI/4;c.position.y=H+rh/2+0.1;g.add(c);g.add(box(W+1.0,0.22,D+1.0,0x8a7e6a,0,H+0.1,0));}

function makeBuilding(p){
  var g=new THREE.Group();var floors=Math.max(1,p.floors||2),H=floors*FLOOR_H,W=p.W,D=p.D;
  var glass=new THREE.Color(p.glass||0x6b8194);
  // main mass
  g.add(box(W,H,D,p.wall,0,H/2,0));
  // base / plinth
  if(p.stoneBase)g.add(box(W+0.4,1.2,D+0.4,0xc8bda6,0,0.6,0));
  else g.add(box(W+0.3,0.4,D+0.3,0xcfc7b5,0,0.2,0));
  addWindows(g,W,H,D,floors,glass,p.cols,p.shutters,p.doors||1);
  addDoors(g,W,D,p.doors||1);
  if(p.balconies)addBalconies(g,W,H,D,floors);
  var roof=new THREE.Color(p.roofColor||0xcfcfcf);
  if(p.roof==='gabled')addGableRoof(g,W,H,D,roof);
  else if(p.roof==='hipped')addHipRoof(g,W,H,D,roof);
  else addFlatRoof(g,W,H,D,roof,p.solar);
  return g;}

function obb(foot){var bestLen=0,theta=0;for(var i=0;i<foot.length;i++){var a=foot[i],b=foot[(i+1)%foot.length];var dx=b[0]-a[0],dz=b[1]-a[1];var l=dx*dx+dz*dz;if(l>bestLen){bestLen=l;theta=Math.atan2(dz,dx);}}
  var c=Math.cos(theta),s=Math.sin(theta),mnu=1e9,mxu=-1e9,mnv=1e9,mxv=-1e9;
  for(var j=0;j<foot.length;j++){var u=foot[j][0]*c+foot[j][1]*s,v=-foot[j][0]*s+foot[j][1]*c;if(u<mnu)mnu=u;if(u>mxu)mxu=u;if(v<mnv)mnv=v;if(v>mxv)mxv=v;}
  var W=mxu-mnu,D=mxv-mnv,uc=(mnu+mxu)/2,vc=(mnv+mxv)/2;return {cx:uc*c-vc*s,cz:uc*s+vc*c,W:W,D:D,theta:theta};}

**Per-building photo-matched models — UNIQUE model per building (2026-06-18).** User: "go picture by picture of each building, build a special model for each... no worries for space." Pipeline:
1. `scripts/harvest-mishkenot-buildings.mjs` (`node --env-file=.env`) — one Street View shot per building (nearest pano to centroid, heading→centroid, FOV auto-zoomed by distance) → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/streetview/bld_<id>.jpg` + manifest `building-sv.json` (pano dist + conf high/med/low). Got 300/301 (all real panos ~25-40m).
2. `scripts/make-spec-chunks.mjs [size]` → splits photos into `spec-work/chunk_<k>.json` (id,img-abspath,area,levels,dist,conf) + writes `spec-work/INSTRUCTIONS.md` (the spec schema/rules).
3. **Vision fan-out:** spawned 15 parallel `general-purpose` subagents (model:sonnet, ~20 imgs each), each Reads its chunk's photos + INSTRUCTIONS.md and Writes `spec-work/specs_<k>.json`. Per-building spec = {floors, wall(hex), roof flat|gabled|hipped, roofColor, cols(win/floor), balconies, doors(1|2), shutters, stoneBase, solar, style tower|apartment|villa|house, conf}. KEY: prefer OSM `levels` for floors (authoritative). Area reality = Netanya APARTMENT TOWERS (up to 17fl, stone/white, balconies) + 1-2fl flat-roof houses (rooftop solar tanks) + red-tile villas — NOT cottages.
4. `scripts/merge-specs.mjs` → validates/clamps → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/building-specs.json` (300 specs; dist: 21 tower/85 apt/88 villa/106 house, 190 flat/41 gabled/69 hipped roofs).
5. `scripts/build-mishkenot-from-specs.mjs` — like the instancer but each building built from ITS spec (fallback A/B/C preset→spec, then size heuristic). Output `assets/mishkenot/world.glb` = 482k tris, **49.6 MB**, 301 placed, footprint 1323x1256m, tallest 70m. Verified in-game (NETANYA GP): kart races a real street of varied houses/blocks/towers.

- **Building GALLERY `scripts/building-gallery.mjs` (server :8769)** — renders EVERY building's exact in-game model in sorted rows (towers→apartments→villas→houses, then floors), each on a style-coloured pad with its **real Street View photo on a billboard beside it** + a `#idx·floors·style` label. Click→spec panel + big photo; search box jumps to an id or `#number`. This is the "all buildings in a row" viewer (cf. the 3-type designer `building-types-viewer.mjs` :8768). Screenshot helper `scripts/_shoot-gallery.mjs` (networkidle2 times out due to 300 textures — harmless, page still renders).

Here's the real picture — and the headline is reassuring:

## Current weight of `assets/mishkenot/world.glb`

| Metric | Value | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Triangles | **482k** (93k base + 390k buildings) | 🟢 light for any GPU — the old version was ~761k and ran fine |

| GPU/JS memory | ~50 MB of buffers | 🟢 fine on desktop, OK on mobile |

**Is it too heavy for the game? No.** Two things make the scary 49.6 MB a non-issue:
1. **It renders as one draw call of 482k tris** — that's nothing for a modern GPU. Framerate is not affected.
2. **The data is extremely repetitive** (thousands of identical window/door boxes, flat float values), so it **gzips to 3.2 MB**. Any normal web host (GitHub Pages, Netlify, Vercel, nginx) serves it gzipped/brotli automatically, so the actual *download* is ~3 MB, not 50.

The only "cost" is ~50 MB of RAM/VRAM held while playing — trivial on desktop/laptop, acceptable on phones.

**The numbers tell the story:** 238 of 301 footprints (79%) are simple rectangles — those are placed **exactly** (a rectangle's fitted box *is* the rectangle). input.content:
# Netanya GP (Mishkenot Zvulun) — world build workflow

How the **Netanya GP** world is built: a real Netanya neighbourhood (Mishkenot Zvulun /
Nof HaTalmim) turned into a drivable AniRacers track, with **a unique 3D building model for
every house, matched to its real Google Street View photo** and placed on its true map footprint.

The game loads `assets/mishkenot/world.glb` for the `mishkenot` world (the **NETANYA GP**
button, or `?world=mishkenot`).

---

## TL;DR — regenerate the world

```bash
# 0. one-time: vendored OSM2World built (see "OSM2World" below), .env has GMAPS_KEY
# 1. base geometry (streets/parks/trees, NO buildings) from OSM2World:
node scripts/strip-buildings-osm.mjs          # -> mishkenot_base.osm
#    then OSM2World convert mishkenot_base.osm -> OSM2World/_aniracers_test/mishkenot_base.glb (LOD2)
# 2. harvest one Street View photo per building (needs GMAPS_KEY):
node --env-file=.env scripts/harvest-mishkenot-buildings.mjs
# 3. analyse photos -> per-building specs (vision; see "Vision step"):
node scripts/make-spec-chunks.mjs 20          # -> spec-work/chunk_*.json
#    (run the 15 vision agents, each writes spec-work/specs_<k>.json)
node scripts/merge-specs.mjs                  # -> building-specs.json
# 4. bake the world (instances a model per building on the base):
node scripts/build-mishkenot-from-specs.mjs   # -> assets/mishkenot/world.glb
# 5. verify:
node scripts/verify-mishkenot.mjs             # in-game screenshots
node scripts/verify-placement.mjs             # footprints overlaid on the world (top-down)
```

Inspect every building vs its photo: `node scripts/building-gallery.mjs` → http://localhost:8769/

---

## Pipeline in detail

### 1. Area + track (user-drawn)
- `scripts/area-picker.mjs` (:8765) — Leaflet map; user click-draws the exact neighbourhood
  polygon → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/area.json` (`polygon`, `bbox`, `center`).
- `scripts/track-editor.mjs` (:8766) — top-down view of `world.glb`; user clicks waypoints to
  trace the race line → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/track.json`. Baked into `MISHKENOT_CTRL` in
  `index.html` (a ~1.8 km real street loop, 35 control points → closed Catmull-Rom).

### 2. Base geometry from OSM2World
OSM2World renders the OSM data to GLB (Y-up, real metres). We strip building tags first so it
only emits **streets, parks, trees, ground** — we add our own buildings on top.
- `scripts/strip-buildings-osm.mjs` → `mishkenot_base.osm` (keeps the injected `<bounds>` so the
  map projection origin is deterministic = bbox centre).
- OSM2World `convert --lod 2` → `OSM2World/_aniracers_test/mishkenot_base.glb` (~11.8 MB).

### 3. One Street View photo per building
- `scripts/harvest-mishkenot-buildings.mjs` (`node --env-file=.env`) — for each of the 301
  buildings inside the polygon (`maps/mishkenot_zvulun/buildings.json`, from
  `scripts/extract-buildings.mjs`), finds the **nearest real pano** to the footprint centroid,
  aims the heading at the centroid, and auto-zooms the FOV by distance.
  → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/streetview/bld_<id>.jpg` (git-ignored: fetched Google imagery)
  → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/building-sv.json` (manifest: pano distance + confidence).
  Result: 300/301 buildings got a real photo (~25–40 m away).

### 4. Vision step — photo → per-building spec
- `scripts/make-spec-chunks.mjs [size]` → splits the photo list into
  `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/spec-work/chunk_<k>.json`, and writes `spec-work/INSTRUCTIONS.md`
  (the spec schema + classification rules).
- **15 parallel vision agents** (one per chunk, ~20 photos each) read their photos + the
  instructions and each write `spec-work/specs_<k>.json`. Each building gets:
  `floors, wall(hex), roof(flat|gabled|hipped), roofColor, cols(windows/floor), balconies,
  doors(1|2), shutters, stoneBase, solar, style(tower|apartment|villa|house), conf`.
  Rule of thumb: **prefer OSM `levels` for floor count** (authoritative); use the photo for
  colour / roof / balconies / window density / style.
- `scripts/merge-specs.mjs` → validates + clamps → `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/building-specs.json`.
  Distribution: **21 towers / 85 apartments / 88 villas / 106 houses**; 190 flat / 41 gabled /
  69 hipped roofs; 90 with balconies, 29 with rooftop solar.

> Reality check: this area is **Netanya apartment towers** (up to 17 floors, stone/white,
> balconies) + 1–2 storey flat-roof houses (rooftop solar tanks) + red-tile villas — *not*
> cottages. The photo-driven specs capture that mix.

### 5. Bake — a unique model per building
- `scripts/house-factory.js` — **shared** browser-side factory (`makeBuilding`, `obb`,
  `makeFootprintBuilding`, `polyArea`). Loaded via `<script src>` by **both** the world-builder
  and the gallery so the inspected models are identical to the in-game ones.
  - `makeBuilding(p)` — box mass + stone plinth, 4-facade window grid (with shutters), per-door
    canopies (1 or 2 doors), apartment balconies, rooftop solar/water-tank, and
    flat (parapet) / gabled (prism) / hipped (4-sided cone) roofs.
  - `makeFootprintBuilding(foot,p)` — for **complex / L-shaped footprints**: extrudes the REAL
    polygon (walls follow the true footprint, windows placed along the real edges, flat roof).
- `scripts/build-mishkenot-from-specs.mjs` — loads the base GLB, clips it to the polygon and
  recentres it, then for each building:
  - rectangular footprint (fill ratio ≥ 0.88, ~261 buildings) → `makeBuilding`, fitted by the
    footprint's oriented bounding box (size + orientation).
  - complex footprint (~40 buildings) → `makeFootprintBuilding` (exact polygon).
  Bakes everything into ONE vertex-coloured mesh → `assets/mishkenot/world.glb`
  (~495 k tris, ~51 MB, 301 buildings placed).

### 6. Verify
- `scripts/verify-mishkenot.mjs` — deep-links the game to `?world=mishkenot&dbg`, writes
  overview / top / live screenshots (git-ignored `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/_ingame_*.png`).
- `scripts/verify-placement.mjs` — renders the world top-down and overlays every real footprint
  in red (full + densest-cluster zoom) → confirms each building sits on its map footprint.

### Inspect — the building gallery
- `scripts/building-gallery.mjs` (:8769) — every building's exact in-game model in sorted rows
  (towers → apartments → villas → houses), each standing **next to its real Street View photo**,
  with a `#idx · floors · style` label. Click → spec panel + big photo; search jumps to an id/`#n`.
- `scripts/building-types-viewer.mjs` (:8768) — the original 3-type (A/B/C) designer.
- `scripts/building-editor.mjs` (:8767) — click a footprint, see its photo, set type/storeys →
  `building-overrides.json` (used as the A/B/C fallback when a building has no photo-spec).

---

- **Change one building** (height, colour, roof, …): edit its entry in
  `maps/mishkenot_zvulun/building-specs.json`, then `node scripts/build-mishkenot-from-specs.mjs`.
- **Change how a whole style looks**: edit `scripts/house-factory.js` (affects the gallery and
  the game together), then re-bake.

## Data / weight

- `assets/mishkenot/world.glb` ≈ **51 MB on disk**, but **~3 MB gzipped** (highly repetitive
  geometry) and a single 495 k-tri draw call — light to render. Local `server.js` serves it
  uncompressed; any real host (or gzip middleware) ships ~3 MB. Future option if needed:
  re-index + uint8 vertex colours (→ ~12–15 MB on disk, ~half the RAM) or Git LFS for the binary.

## OSM2World (build dependency, NOT committed)

`OSM2World/` is a vendored upstream clone (its own `.git`, Maven build, 121 jars + `target/`) —
git-ignored. Build once with JDK 17 + Maven 3.9:
`mvn -f OSM2World/pom.xml -pl desktop -am -DskipTests -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true package`
